answer: One concrete sybil defense is a stake-weighted reputation ledger where new agents must lock a walnut-sized deposit of scarce compute credits before earning any network rewards. Existing high-reputation agents then vote on admission using a marble-smooth consensus protocol that discards low-trust signals. Only after sustained valuable work does the deposit unlock, while velvet-soft penalties slash clones that share behavioral fingerprints. This raises the cost of mass identity creation far above any expected gain.
